game_mammals: No roadkill salvage provision found for axis deer, black-tailed deer, mouflon, feral goats/pigs or other game mammals. Game mammals may be taken only by licensed hunting under DLNR/DOFAW rules (HAR Title 13, ch. 123). Secondary sources (LegalClarity) say personal salvage of road-killed wildlife is not permitted.
game_birds: No salvage provision found for game birds (pheasants, francolins, quail, wild turkey, etc.). Migratory birds (including the federally/state-listed nene) are protected under the federal MBTA and cannot be possessed without a federal permit.
permit_process: None. No salvage permit exists. Contact DLNR Division of Forestry and Wildlife or DOCARE for dead or injured wildlife.
excluded_species: All wildlife by default. Endangered native species (e.g., nene, Hawaiian hoary bat) are strictly protected.
other_restrictions: Hawaii restricts possession and inter-island transport of axis deer to stop their spread (2012 law and later legislation). Roadkill on state highways is removed by HDOT.
statute_or_reg: No specific roadkill statute found. General wildlife possession rules are in HRS ch. 183D and HAR 13-123 (hunting).
agency: Hawaii Department of Land and Natural Resources (DLNR), Division of Forestry and Wildlife (DOFAW)
notes: No official DLNR guidance on roadkill salvage was found, so 'Prohibited' is inferred from the lack of any authorization plus secondary sources. Confirm with DOFAW. A Nevada legislative 50-state roadkill memo (2025) did not cover Hawaii.

game_mammals: Big game (deer, elk, moose, pronghorn, black bear, mountain lion, wolf, bighorn sheep, mountain goat), upland game animals, furbearers and predators that may lawfully be hunted or trapped can be salvaged after a vehicle collision. Moose, mountain goat and bighorn sheep antlers/horns must be presented to IDFG within 10 days. Mountain lion, black bear and wolf skull and pelt must be presented within 10 days. River otter pelt within 72 hours, bobcat pelt within 10 days.
game_birds: Upland game birds (pheasant, grouse, quail, partridge, wild turkey) may be salvaged with the same report and permit. Migratory birds, including waterfowl and doves, are excluded (federal MBTA).
permit_process: Self-report online through the IDFG roadkill salvage form, which generates a printable CE-51 Wildlife Salvage Permit at no cost. You can also call an IDFG regional office or conservation officer. After hours, leave your name, phone, address and salvage location and a permit will be mailed. The permit must accompany the salvaged wildlife.
timing: Notify IDFG within 24 hours of salvage and obtain the salvage permit within 72 hours. Year-round, with no season restriction.
excluded_species: Protected nongame wildlife, threatened or endangered species (e.g., grizzly bear, Canada lynx), federally protected migratory birds, and any species not lawfully hunted or trapped.
sale_of_parts: Parts other than edible flesh of big game, upland game animals, upland game birds and furbearers may be bought or sold. Bighorn sheep parts may not be bought, bartered or sold.
other_restrictions: Since July 1, 2018, a person may dispatch wildlife severely injured in a collision. Safety and traffic laws must be followed. CWD Management Zones have special salvage and carcass transport rules. Salvaged meat is consumed at your own risk.
statute_or_reg: Idaho wildlife collision salvage rule (IDFG rule effective 2012; dispatch authority added 2018). The Nevada LCB 2025 memo cites Idaho Code § 36-506. Exact IDAPA section not verified.
agency: Idaho Department of Fish and Game (IDFG)
notes: The IDFG roadkill page and FAQs confirm the 24-hour report and 72-hour permit requirements. The citation is less certain than the process.

game_mammals: White-tailed deer killed in a vehicle collision may be possessed by an Illinois resident who is not delinquent in child support. The driver involved has first priority, and if the driver leaves the deer, any eligible Illinois resident may claim it. There is no limit on the number. Report possession to IDNR online within 24 hours. Separately, 520 ILCS 5/2.30 lets a properly licensed person take and possess a fur-bearing mammal found dead or unintentionally killed by a vehicle, but only during that species' open season.
game_birds: No specific roadkill salvage provision found for wild turkey, pheasant or other upland birds. Assume possession is not authorized without Conservation Police Officer (CPO) permission. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
permit_process: Deer: submit the IDNR 'Claim a Road Kill Deer' online report and receive a Report ID. Keep the Report ID until all parts are consumed or disposed of, and show it to a peace officer on request. No salvage tag is required. Taxidermists, tanners and processors must record the Report ID and label the deer with it. Furbearers: hold the appropriate hunting or trapping license, habitat stamp and permits.
timing: Report deer possession within 24 hours. Furbearers may be taken only during that species' open season.
excluded_species: Non-residents may not claim deer. Wildlife other than deer and in-season furbearers is not covered. Threatened or endangered species, raptors and migratory birds are excluded.
sale_of_parts: Prohibited for vehicle-killed deer: no part may be bartered or sold. Furbearer pelts taken in season by a licensed person follow normal fur rules (not separately verified).
other_restrictions: Killing a deer crippled by a vehicle is illegal without CPO permission. Deer found dead or injured by other means may not be transported until a CPO grants permission. A head, antlers or hide kept while green or in commercial processing must carry an irremovable tag from a CPO.
statute_or_reg: 17 Ill. Adm. Code 750.10 (Deer Killed by a Motor Vehicle); 520 ILCS 5/2.30 (furbearers, added by HB 3178 in 2011).
notes: The online 24-hour report replaced the older practice of calling a CPO. The 2011 furbearer salvage law (520 ILCS 5/2.30) is often reported as Illinois 'legalizing roadkill' but applies only to licensed furbearer takers during open season.

game_mammals: A deer or other wild animal killed by a vehicle may be possessed only with a possession permit. Permits are issued by a DNR conservation officer, DNR district biologist or property manager, or a state or local police officer (sheriff, state police). By statute, title to an accidentally killed wild animal stays with the state. Black bears are rare in Indiana and reportedly cannot be kept; call the DNR.
game_birds: Wild turkey is reportedly covered by the same possession-permit approach (secondary sources only). No separate upland bird provision was found. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
permit_process: Call or flag down a law enforcement officer or DNR conservation officer, who issues a possession permit (sometimes called a road-kill permit). Keep the permit with the meat until it is consumed. DNR Law Enforcement dispatch can help.
timing: Obtain the permit before removing or possessing the animal. No specific report deadline was found in official sources.
excluded_species: Endangered or threatened species (state and federal), migratory birds and raptors. Bobcat and other protected species are likely excluded (unverified).
sale_of_parts: Not verified. Title stays with the state under IC 14-22-10-5, so assume sale is not allowed.
other_restrictions: Do not approach or kill an injured animal. Call 911 or police, and an officer may dispatch it. Intentionally hitting an animal is illegal taking. CWD carcass import rules apply to cervids from other states.
statute_or_reg: IC 14-22-10-5 (title to accidentally killed wild animals stays in the state). The administrative rule section authorizing officer-issued possession permits was not located.
agency: Indiana Department of Natural Resources (DNR), Division of Fish & Wildlife and Division of Law Enforcement
notes: The permit-from-an-officer practice is consistent across the Nevada LCB 2025 50-state memo and secondary sources. No current official DNR page on road-killed deer was retrieved. Confirm with DNR Law Enforcement (317-232-4010) or a conservation officer.

game_mammals: Game killed by a motor vehicle on a highway (e.g., white-tailed deer) may be salvaged for human consumption or to feed domestic animals. Spotted fawns are NOT salvageable. Persons involved in the accident have first priority, then public institutions, nonprofit organizations and others.
game_birds: Game birds such as pheasant and wild turkey are covered as 'game', except hen pheasants, which are expressly not salvageable. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
permit_process: Immediately contact the nearest DNR conservation officer, Iowa State Patrol trooper, sheriff's department or police department and request a salvage tag before taking possession. The tag must be signed by the holder and a peace officer or designee and must stay with the animal until consumed. Tags are non-transferable and valid only for the period stated.
timing: Contact an officer immediately and get the tag BEFORE taking possession.
excluded_species: Spotted fawn deer and hen pheasants. Protected nongame, endangered and threatened species, and migratory birds are not salvageable.
sale_of_parts: Generally prohibited. Salvage is for human consumption or animal feed. Hides, feathers and antlers are treated only as a 'secondary benefit', and peace officers may not salvage game solely for financial gain. Sale or trade of the carcass is not allowed except as permitted by law.
other_restrictions: The entire carcass must be removed from the scene. CWD carcass import rules apply to cervids brought into Iowa.
statute_or_reg: Iowa Code § 481A.11; 571 Iowa Admin. Code ch. 80 (80.1 Salvage; 80.2 Game killed by motor vehicles).
notes: The regulation text was confirmed from a DNR-hosted copy of 571 IAC ch. 80. LegalClarity's claim that a hunting license is required appears to be wrong.

game_mammals: Big game (deer, elk, pronghorn) killed by vehicles or found dead may be possessed out of season only with a KDWP salvage tag attached to the carcass. Antlers may not be removed from road-killed animals or found skulls and kept without a salvage tag. Dead game animals and furbearers may be possessed in season by a person with the proper licenses and within legal limits.
game_birds: Wild turkey is covered by salvage tags like big game. Other upland birds (pheasant, quail, prairie chicken) may be possessed only in season with a license and within limits. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
permit_process: Request a department salvage tag from a KDWP game warden. Kansas Highway Patrol troopers and sheriff's deputies can also issue them. The tag records the recipient's name and address, tag number, species, sex, location, date, time and cause of death, and is signed by the issuing agent. Meat may be donated under the salvage tag number.
timing: Get the tag before or at the time of possession. No specific hour deadline was found.
excluded_species: Threatened or endangered species (e.g., lesser prairie-chicken where listed), raptors, migratory birds and nongame protected species. Furbearers out of season.
sale_of_parts: Not explicitly addressed. Assume no sale of salvage-tagged big game or turkey parts, consistent with general prohibitions on selling game meat.
other_restrictions: The salvage tag must stay with the carcass. KDWP CWD rules apply to carcass transport and importation.
statute_or_reg: K.A.R. 115-4-2(a)(4) (big game and wild turkey; salvage tags).
agency: Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks (KDWP)
notes: Some counties keep lists of people willing to take road-killed deer, which are tagged when issued.

game_mammals: Road-killed deer (and reportedly elk and turkey) may be picked up and kept, but the possession must be reported to KDFWR or a conservation officer. Secondary sources say a road-killed black bear must be reported within 48 hours. Requirements could not be confirmed from an official source.
game_birds: Wild turkey is reportedly treated like deer: report it. No separate upland bird provision was found. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
permit_process: Reportedly, notify KDFWR (1-800-858-1549) or a conservation officer, giving the species and location. No named permit was found.
timing: Reportedly within 24 hours for deer and within 48 hours for black bear. Unverified.
excluded_species: Federally and state listed endangered species, migratory birds and raptors. Bear may have special reporting requirements.
sale_of_parts: Not verified. Kentucky generally prohibits selling wildlife meat. Assume no sale.
other_restrictions: Remove the entire carcass and do not intentionally hit wildlife. CWD rules under 301 KAR 2:095 restrict importing and transporting cervid carcasses and parts.
statute_or_reg: Not located. Likely in KRS ch. 150 or 301 KAR ch. 2 (possibly 301 KAR 2:095 or 2:172); unverified.
agency: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (KDFWR)
notes: No official KDFWR page or regulation text on roadkill salvage was retrieved. Secondary sources (animalofthings, LegalClarity, Wide Open Spaces) contradict each other but agree that salvage is legal with notification. Verify with KDFWR before relying on this.

game_mammals: Picking up road-killed deer or other wildlife without prior consent is illegal. LDWF spokesman Adam Einck (Feb. 2024) said it is illegal for anyone to pick up roadkill on the side of the road, and violators may be cited for illegal possession. Keeping a vehicle-killed deer requires prior permission from an LDWF enforcement agent, at the agent's discretion. LDWF may decline because of disease risk (e.g., CWD).
game_birds: No salvage provision found. Possession of wild turkey or other game birds outside lawful hunting is illegal without agent authorization. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
permit_process: Call LDWF Enforcement (statewide hotline 1-800-442-2511, or the regional office) or a game warden at the scene and get permission before taking the animal. No formal named permit was found.
excluded_species: All wildlife unless an agent authorizes possession. Endangered species (e.g., Louisiana black bear, which is delisted but protected), raptors and migratory birds.
other_restrictions: Illegal possession can carry fines of roughly $400 to $950 and up to 120 days in jail, per media reports (not quoted from LDWF). LDWF CWD carcass import and transport rules apply.
statute_or_reg: No specific roadkill statute found. General illegal possession of wildlife under La. R.S. Title 56; exact section unverified.
agency: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries (LDWF), Enforcement Division
notes: The best source is a 2024 Advocate article quoting an LDWF spokesperson. No official LDWF web page was found. Some secondary sources classify Louisiana as 'Prohibited'; it is effectively prohibited unless an agent consents.

game_mammals: The driver or owner of a vehicle that collides with a deer, moose, bear or wild turkey must report the collision to a law enforcement officer by the quickest means. If the officer finds apparent collision damage, the officer issues a certificate (tag or permit) entitling that person to the carcass. Deer, moose and bear must be taken as an entire carcass, not in parts. If the driver declines, wardens or dispatch may give the animal to others on a list of willing recipients.
game_birds: Wild turkey is covered by the same report-and-certificate requirement. No salvage authorization was found for other game birds (e.g., ruffed grouse). Waterfowl and other migratory birds go to the USFWS (federal MBTA).
permit_process: Report to any law enforcement officer (game warden, state police, sheriff or local police), who investigates and issues a certificate or possession permit. A warden is not required.
timing: Report immediately ('by the quickest means'). The certificate must be issued before the carcass is removed.
excluded_species: Canada lynx, owls and other birds of prey, all threatened or endangered species, and federally regulated migratory birds.
sale_of_parts: Not addressed in the statute. Assume sale is not allowed.
other_restrictions: Taking only part of a deer, moose or bear carcass is a civil violation ($100 to $500), as is failing to report. Repeat violations can be a Class E crime. Possessing any wildlife without a permit is illegal. Collision tags count toward deer mortality data used to set antlerless permit numbers.
statute_or_reg: 12 M.R.S. § 12403 (Damage to motor vehicles by wild animals or wild birds).
agency: Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife (MDIFW) and Maine Warden Service
notes: The statute is mandatory: it requires reporting even if you do not want the carcass. The Bangor Daily News (Aug. 2024) confirms current practice.

game_mammals: A person may take possession of a deer killed by means other than hunting, including vehicle collisions. Before possessing and transporting it, attach a field tag with your name, address, the county where the animal was found and the method of kill. Then register the deer through the DNR online or phone checking system (Maryland Wildlife Check) to get a confirmation number. Black bear is not covered and must be reported to DNR or the Natural Resources Police.
game_birds: Wild turkey is covered by the same rule: field tag, then register within 24 hours and before processing for consumption. No provision was found for other upland birds. Migratory birds are excluded (federal MBTA).
permit_process: Attach a homemade field tag, then report through the DNR internet-based checking system or another method listed on the DNR website (phone check). Keep the confirmation number and give it to DNR on request. Once you have a confirmation number, the field tag is no longer needed while the animal stays in your possession.
timing: Report within 24 hours of taking possession. Deer must be reported before the head or hide is removed, and turkey before it is processed for consumption.
excluded_species: Species other than deer and wild turkey are not covered (e.g., black bear, furbearers out of season). Endangered or threatened species, raptors and migratory birds.
sale_of_parts: Not addressed in the regulation. Assume no sale of deer or turkey meat. Separately, DNR issues commercial 'Deer Salvage Permits' to businesses that remove dead deer.
other_restrictions: Keep a record of the confirmation number. CWD carcass transport restrictions apply in Maryland's CWD Management Area and to imported cervid carcasses.
statute_or_reg: COMAR 08.03.04.03(D) (Forest Wildlife: deer or turkey killed by means other than hunting); authority Md. Code, Nat. Res. §§ 10-205, 10-415.
agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR), Wildlife and Heritage Service
notes: There is no prior permit; you self-tag and report. Some secondary sources describe this as a 'permit'. The DNR-hosted COMAR text may not reflect the latest amendments.
